questions.question: Where is Havelock Island, a popular tourist destination located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

__
 
• **Havelock Island **is located east of the **Andaman Islands **and is administered by the **Nicobar Islands administration.**
 
• It was named for** British General Henry Havelock**, who lived in the area when India was a British colony.
 
• Govinda Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Radha Nagar, Shyam Nagar, and Bejoy Nagar are five prominent settlements on Havelock Island, each with its own beaches and lovely shorelines.
 
• According to reports, the island is home to the majority of the island's immigrant population from Myanmar and Bengal.
 
• As a memorial to Subhash Chandra Bose, the island was renamed Swaraj Dweep in 2018.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose flew the national flag on the island in 1943, naming Andaman Island Shaheed Dweep and Nicobar Island Swaraj Dweep, before India's independence.

• The Andaman Sea separates the area from Thailand and Myanmar, around 150 kilometres north of Aceh, Indonesia.
 
• It is divided into two island groups, the Andaman Islands (partly) and the Nicobar Islands, by the 150-kilometre-long Ten Degree Channel, with the Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south.

questions.question: Which of the following universities was founded by the Pala rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikramasila.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramasila University** was founded by the **Pala dynasty rulers** in the **8th century CE**, in present-day Bihar, India.
 
• The university was a major center for **Buddhist studies,** attracting scholars from all over India and other countries like** Tibet, China, and Korea.**
 
• The university had several faculties, including **philosophy, logic, grammar, and medicine**, and its curriculum emphasized both theoretical and practical aspects of learning.
 
• Vikramasila University declined in the **12th century** CE due to invasions by **Turkish armies** and a shift in patronage towards other centers of learning like **Nalanda and Odantapuri.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nalanda University** is located in present-day **Bihar, India.**

 
 
• It was founded in the **5th century CE **and became a renowned center for **Buddhist studies** and other disciplines like **astronomy, mathematics, and logic.**
 
• It had a vast campus, with several** temples, libraries, and lecture halls**, and attracted scholars and students from all over Asia.
 
• The university was destroyed by **Turkish invaders** in the **12th century **CE, and its ruins were rediscovered in the** 19th century** CE.
 
 
 
• **Valabhi University **is located in present-day **Gujarat, **India.
 
 
• It was founded in the **6th century CE **and became a major center for** Jain studies** and other disciplines like grammar, medicine, and astronomy.
 
• It had a well-organized curriculum and a **large library **and attracted students from all over India and other countries like** Sri Lanka and China.**
 
• The university declined in the** 8th century CE **due to political instability and invasions by Arab armies.
 
 
 
• **Taxila University** is located in present-day **Pakistan.**
 
 
• It was founded in the** 5th century BCE** and became a renowned center for **Buddhist and Hindu **studies, as well as other disciplines like medicine, astronomy, and philosophy.
 
• It had several faculties and a diverse student population, including** Greeks, Persians, and Chinese.**
 
• The university declined in the **5th century CE **due to political turmoil and invasions by Huns and other nomadic tribes.

questions.question: Which of the following villages is related to the ‘Bhoodan Movement’ initiated by Vinoba Bhave?

• **Vinoba Bhave**, a follower of** Mahatma Gandhi,** founded the** Bhoodan Movement **in **Pochampally village in April 1951.**
 
• The Movement made an effort to persuade **wealthy landowners **to voluntarily **donate a portion of their property** to others who were **without land.**
 
• Bhave was philosophically influenced by **Gram Swarajya and the Sarvodaya movement** of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• About** 1.9 million hectares** were collected in **just six years.**
 
• Over the **next two decades **the movement took shape of a law called the **Bhoodan Act** and put the **government in charge** of distributing land from the land bank.
 
• Later, the movement evolved into the **Gramdan (village in gift) movement**, when the entirety or a significant portion of a **village's land was donated** by at least **75%** of the locals for equal distribution among all villagers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Where is the Vivekanand Rock Memorial situated?

• The memorial was built in **1970 **in honor of **Swami Vivekananda** who is said to have attained enlightenment on the rock.
 
• It consists of two main structures - the **Vivekananda Mandapam** and the **Shripada Mandapam**.
 
• The memorial is a popular tourist destination and a place of pilgrimage.

• **Swami Vivekananda** was a key figure in the introduction of Indian philosophies of **Vedanta and Yoga** to the Western world.
 
• He is also credited with raising interfaith awareness, bringing Hinduism to the status of a major world religion during the late 19th century.

• In ancient India, bricks were often sun-dried before being fired for additional strength.
 
• The durability of bricks made them a preferred choice for long-lasting constructions.

questions.question: Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar?

• It is located on** Ashok Rajpath** between Sultanganj and Alamganj.

• The central dome is supported by** four arches**.
 
• The mosque is a fine example of Mughal architecture.
 
• Pathar Ki Masjid is a beautiful and historic mosque that is an important part of the cultural heritage of Patna.
 
• It is a popular tourist destination and a place of worship for the Muslim community.

questions.question: Buland Darwaza located in Fatehpur Sikri is the entrance gate of which of the following mosques?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jama Masjid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Buland Darwaza **serves as the primary entrance to the **Jama Masjid located in Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• It known as** "Door of Victory," **it was constructed by the **Mughal emperor Akbar in 1575** to commemorate his triumph over Gujarat.
 
• Renowned for its Mughal architecture, the Buland Darwaza stands as the world's tallest gateway, soaring at a height of 53.63 meters and spanning 35 meters in width, accessible via 42 steps.
 
• The Jama Masjid, a magnificent mosque, was completed in 1571.
 
• It features a central nave, along with two colonnaded halls and two square chambers crowned by domes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Jama Masjid **is a 16th-century congregational mosque situated within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Fatehpur Sikri, located in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• Constructed by the Mughal emperor Akbar, it held the distinction of being the largest mosque within the empire during its construction period.
 
• Drawing inspiration from earlier mosques built by various pre-Mughal sultanates, the Jama Masjid served as a significant influence on subsequent Mughal architectural styles.
 
• Within the mosque complex, notable monuments include the Buland Darwaza, which functions as the southern gateway to the mosque, and the Tomb of Salim Chishti.
 
• This tomb is dedicated to the revered saint Salim Chishti, in whose honor the mosque was originally erected.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian state has the famous tourist destination called Pamban Island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Pamban Island **is a **famous **tourist **destination **in the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.

 
 
• Although this **exotic island** is **not **a **part of mainland India**, yet is a **popular tourist destination**.
 
• **Pamban **Island is a part of the **Ramanathapuram district **of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **Pamban **Island is the** largest island in Tamil Nadu i**n terms of area and is known **worldwide **for the popular **pilgrimage **site **Rameshwaram**.
 
• **Rameshwaram **is the** holy place** in the** Hindu text**, as it is believed that **Lord Rama built a bridge of stones** across the sea to rescue his wife Sita from the demon king of Lanka, Ravana. 
 
• **Pamban Island **is located between the **Indian Peninsula **and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Pamban **Island is **connected **to **mainland **India via the **Pamban channel**.
 
• **Pamban rail bridge **is **India’s first sea bridge **built in **1914 **and is **2065m** long.
 
 
• The **bridge **was made to **connect **the **Ramanathapuram **district in Tamil Nadu to **Pamban Island**.
 
• The** bridge can open **up to let the **ferry boats**, and **ships pass**.
 
 
 
• **Rama Setu **or **Adam’s bridge** is another **tourist attraction** for tourists who visit Pamban Island.
 
 
• As per popular beliefs, the bridge **starts **from **Dhanuskodi **and terminates at **Mannar Island** in Sri Lanka.
 
• The **bridge **is made of **limestone shoals**, which make them **float **on the **water surface**.
